title: Canary-quality variance mitigation and customer escalation playbook across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Maya Chen
description: Playbook and working notes for detecting, classifying, mitigating, and coordinating customer communications when a canary rollout shows quality regressions or functional failures across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
steps: 1) Detect: enrich monitoring alarms to include quality deltas (eval-set regressions, semantic drift alerts) in addition to latency/errors
2) Classify: triage whether regression is model-quality, infra-induced (quantization/kernel issue), prompt/format change, or dataset/serving mismatch
3) Contain: apply immediate traffic isolation - float canary to 0% or split-traffic to fallback model variant depending on customer SLA and capacity
4) Fix: hotpatch configuration, apply model artifact rollback, or deploy compatibility adapter for prompt changes
5) Validate: run golden prompt set + customer repro cases in staging that mirrors the customer environment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), confirm fix on metrics and manual review
6) Rollout: staged reintroduction with 1) weighted rollout with progressive checks or 2) full rollback if sustained failure
7) Postmortem: timeline, RCA, corrective actions, and updates to automated canary tests and alarms
rollback_plan: Immediate fallback: route traffic away from canary to the previous stable model artifact for Hosted and Dedicated via routing policy (fast path)
Private deployments: coordinate with customer ops - offer signed hotfix binary or a configuration toggle; default to documented customer roll-forward/rollback instructions in Private runbook
Weighted rollback: if customer traffic is mixed, apply canary weight to 0% and ramp older model to 100% with automated validation checks before confirming
Data plane incompatibility: if a model-level format or KV-cache incompatibility exists, block automated rollback and execute isolation with node drains and kernel-profile restoration
communication_plan: Tiered notification: oncall -> ENG incident lead -> PM & Solutions -> Account exec
Customer message templates: initial acknowledgement within 30 minutes, status updates every 60 minutes while active, resolution summary within 24h
Dedicated/Private customers: include recommended immediate mitigations (switch to pinned stable model, increase timeout/latency buffer) and offer assisted rollback session
Public status: update status.redwood.ai when Hosted is impacted and issue affects multiple customers
Post-resolution: share RCA and next steps, offer follow-up verification window and credit where appropriate
acceptance_criteria: Playbook used in at least two incident drills covering Hosted and Dedicated paths
Runbook pages created/updated for Private rollout instructions and signed off by Solutions Engineering
Automated canary checks added to CI for the top 5 customer prompt sets and run on every model push
Communication templates validated with GTM and legal for enterprise disclosures
notes: Trade-offs discussed: weighted rollback reduces blast radius but requires healthy capacity for older model; full rollback is faster but may produce availability hiccups if rollback path causes infra churn
Decision: default to weighted rollback for Hosted/Dedicated unless customer explicitly requests immediate full rollback
For Private, assume customer-controlled network; prepare both signed artifact and step-by-step rollback checklist to minimize phone support time
We will not rely solely on token-level error rates; incorporate semantic evaluation automated by eval-harness to detect quality regressions
